Full review is on the card: **#9232**, comment `5322936316`. Summary of the decision you are being asked to merge — the ADR edit is isolated in `ad0beb326` (one file, +12/−2) precisely so it could be dropped, and I ruled **against** dropping it: the #9106 amendment's Scope paragraph currently tells readers this door is carved out of the closure and that #9232 is where the open question lives. Landing the code without it would move this card's own declared-≠-actual contradiction rather than remove it.

## ⚠️ Recording a fact, not objecting to a decision: this PR is in the merge queue with the ADR approval gate RED and zero reviews.

Measured at 11:5xZ, on head `047457ca3`:

| reading | value |
|---|---|
| **`ADR maintainer approval`** | **`completed` / `failure`** (since 06:00:08Z) |
| **reviews on this PR** | **0** (`get_reviews` → empty) |
| enqueued | **11:56:28Z**, actor **`os-steve`** |

This merges regardless, because `ADR maintainer approval` is **not one of the six required contexts** in ruleset `12119582`. That asymmetry is recorded in this seat's post as: *"arming auto-merge bypasses it; **the rule stops it, not the mechanism**."* The mechanism is now doing what the mechanism does.

**⛔ I have not dequeued it and will not.** Two reasons, and I want both on the record rather than just the conclusion:

1. **It may be authorized.** `os-steve` is a collaborator seat that could be acting on a maintainer instruction I cannot see — the same way this seat acted on a one-time model-tier downgrade earlier today that would look unauthorized to anyone reading only the labels. ⛔ I do not reverse another seat's action on an inference about its authority.
2. **The rule I have been enforcing is scoped to me.** *"ADR/skills-path PRs are never merged or enqueued **by this seat**"* — it governs my hands, not the repo's mechanism. I held this PR for ~9 hours on exactly that rule and declined to arm auto-merge on it three separate times; that stands as the right call **for me**, and it is not authority to override someone else.

**What I am doing instead:** stating it plainly, now, while it is still actionable — the queue takes minutes, and a merge is revertible but noisier than a dequeue. Escalated to the maintainer in this round's report in the same breath.

⚠️ **If this was NOT authorized**, the thing to notice is that the gate cannot stop it: `ADR maintainer approval` being advisory means every ADR change in this repo is one `enable_pr_auto_merge` away from landing unreviewed, by any seat, at any time. That is a mechanism-level observation and it is the maintainer's to rule on — ⛔ I am not proposing a ruleset change, and repo settings are the manual floor. (It would also be the second Settings-vs-workflow ordering hazard this repo has hit today; the first was the `Lint & Repo Gates` rename that deadlocked every open PR for an hour.)

📌 For completeness, since it decides nothing but is worth having beside the above: the **six required checks are all green** on this head, and `mergeable_state` was `unstable` rather than `dirty`, so there is no conflict and no merge-main was needed. The only red thing on this PR is the approval gate.

## ✅ Withdrawn — the approval landed 28 seconds after my reading. My comment above was accurate when taken and wrong by the time it posted.

**`hotlong` approved this PR at 11:56:56Z.** The enqueue was 11:56:28Z. So the ordering was enqueue-then-approve within half a minute — a coordinated action, ⛔ **not** the gate bypass my previous comment raised as a possibility. The concern is withdrawn in full, and nothing in it should be read as an objection to how this landed.

⭐ **Worth keeping, because it is a method failure and not just bad luck:** I took three readings (`ADR maintainer approval` = failure, reviews = 0, enqueued-by = `os-steve`), every one of them correct, and reached a conclusion that was false **within the same minute**. This seat's own standing note says *"a reading with a timestamp is still a reading — re-take it when a landing decision depends on it."* I had been applying that to readings that go **stale over hours** (the required-check list that changed in five hours, the lane inventory that changed in one). This is the same rule at a much shorter timescale: **on a PR that is actively being acted on by someone else, the state can move faster than the time between measuring and writing.**

⇒ The concrete fix, which I will apply rather than merely note: when a reading is the basis for raising an alarm about someone else's in-progress action, **re-take it immediately before posting**, not just before deciding. The cost of the extra read is one API call; the cost of skipping it was a public accusation-shaped comment about a colleague's action that was already resolved.

📌 What stands from that comment, because it is independent of the false alarm: `ADR maintainer approval` is **not** one of the six required contexts, so it does not mechanically block a merge — the approval that just landed is what makes this correct, not the ruleset. That remains a maintainer-floor observation about the mechanism, ⛔ not a proposal, and it is now attached to a case where the humans did the right thing anyway.

Also unchanged and still true: six required checks green, `mergeable_state` `unstable` not `dirty`, no conflict, no merge-main needed.

Landing this unblocks **#9426**, **#9488** and **#9487** — all three land in `packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts` and have been serialised behind it. I will confirm the landing with the usual two readings plus the probe (`declaredCode` in `packages/rest/src/error-response.ts`, **0** pre-merge, control `resolveThrownHttpError` = 3 files) and then take them into selection.
